headline: Law puts about 40 acres at Wounded Knee, South Dakota, into protected status for two Sioux tribes as a memorial and sacred site.
what_it_does: The law directs the Department of the Interior to place about 40 acres of land in Oglala Lakota County, South Dakota, into restricted fee status for the Oglala Sioux Tribe and the Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe. Under this status, the tribes own the land, but federal law limits selling it, transferring it, or placing liens, leases, or rights-of-way on it. The land must be kept as a memorial and sacred site, following a 2022 agreement between the two tribes. Commercial development and gaming are not allowed on the land.

who_it_affects.how: The tribe will share ownership of the land, which must be kept as a memorial and sacred site under limits on selling or using it.
